text: "The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He sees the Father do." Jesus ministered from what He saw.
explanation:
At the pool of Bethesda lay "a great multitude of sick people," yet Jesus healed one man, who'd been ill for thirty-eight years. Healing is for all, and everyone who touched Him was made well. But when He went to someone on His own initiative, He followed what the Father showed Him. "Most assuredly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He sees the Father do."

Jesus lived as a man anointed by the Spirit, and He's our pattern. "For the Father loves the Son, and shows Him all things that He Himself does; and He will show Him greater works than these, that you may marvel." Ask your Father to show you too, and expect to marvel this year.

text: Habakkuk said, "I will watch to see what He will say to me." God answered, "Write the vision and make it plain."
explanation:
Habakkuk was troubled by the violence and injustice around him: "O Lord, how long shall I cry, and You will not hear?" Instead of stewing, he positioned himself: "I will stand my watch… and watch to see what He will say to me." Not "hear": see. And God answered: "Write the vision and make it plain on tablets, that he may run who reads it. For the vision is yet for an appointed time… though it tarries, wait for it."

Set aside time away from the noise, with a notebook ready. That's an act of faith. Write down what He shows you: a verse, a phrase, a picture. Years later, those pages will build your faith. Run with what you've seen.

text: "All the land which you see I give to you." The provision is in the vision.
explanation:
After Lot separated from him, God told Abram, "Lift your eyes now and look… northward, southward, eastward, and westward; for all the land which you see I give to you and your descendants forever." What he saw, he received. Even the word provision contains vision.

A vision from God isn't bound by time. He shows you the end as though it's already done, and you can enjoy it now while you wait for it to manifest. Moses "endured as seeing Him who is invisible," and at 120 his eyes weren't dim nor his strength gone. See Jesus first; in Him, everything else is secured.

text: Blinded Saul was praying, and saw a vision of a man named Ananias, "grace of God." Grace was the first face he saw.
explanation:
After meeting the risen Jesus on the Damascus road, Saul was blind for three days. The Lord told a disciple named Ananias, "Behold, he is praying. And in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in and putting his hand on him, so that he might receive his sight." Ananias, Hananiah in Hebrew, means "the Lord is gracious."

While his physical eyes were closed, Saul's heart saw grace coming. And when the scales fell, the first person he saw was "grace of God," the theme of his whole life's message. Notice that Peter, Cornelius and Paul all received visions while praying. Pray, and watch.

text: See your disease on Jesus' body on the cross. From that moment, it begins to wither from the roots.
explanation:
When Israel was bitten by serpents, they were told to look at the bronze serpent on the pole, not at their wounds. "As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up." A loving parent would take their child's sickness if they could. Jesus did: "Surely He has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows."

So picture it: that growth, that pressure, that condition, on His body on the cross, not yours. When Jesus cursed the fig tree, it still looked green that day, but the next morning it was "dried up from the roots." Things may look the same at first. Keep seeing it on Him.

text: Grace is attracted to your weaknesses, not your highlight reel.
explanation:
We post our best moments and hide our weak ones, then scroll through everyone else's highlights and feel our lives are miserable by comparison. But Jesus said, "My grace is sufficient for you, for My strength is made perfect in weakness."

His power can't flow through the parts where you're relying on your own strength. It flows through the cracks. That's why Paul could say, "When I am weak, then I am strong." If you have a lot of weaknesses, you're a candidate for a lot of His power.

text: "Your young men shall see visions, your old men shall dream dreams": pictures are the language of the Spirit.
explanation:
On the day of Pentecost, Peter announced, "This is what was spoken by the prophet Joel… I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh… your young men shall see visions, your old men shall dream dreams." A dream is a picture while you sleep; a vision is a picture while you're awake. Both are the Spirit's language, and they're for the new covenant, for these last days.

Yes, false visions exist. But a bride and groom don't spend their wedding studying grounds for divorce. Don't let fear of the counterfeit rob you of the real. When God fills you with His Spirit, expect Him to speak in pictures, and learn His language.
